hints.title: Greedy Maximal Base
hints.text: Taking the k largest numbers provides the absolute maximum sum possible for length k.

hints.title: Parity Discrepancy Adjustment
hints.text: If the top k sum is odd, changing the parity requires replacing one odd with an even or one even with an odd.

hints.title: Minimal Delta Replacement
hints.text: Compare swapping the smallest chosen odd for the largest unused even versus the smallest chosen even for the largest unused odd.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def largestEvenSum(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        nums.sort(reverse=True)
        chosen = nums[:k]
        curr_sum = sum(chosen)

        if curr_sum % 2 == 0:
            return curr_sum

        min_odd_chosen = min((x for x in chosen if x % 2 == 1), default=None)
        min_even_chosen = min((x for x in chosen if x % 2 == 0), default=None)

        rest = nums[k:]
        max_even_rest = max((x for x in rest if x % 2 == 0), default=None)
        max_odd_rest = max((x for x in rest if x % 2 == 1), default=None)

        ans = -1
        if min_odd_chosen is not None and max_even_rest is not None:
            ans = max(ans, curr_sum - min_odd_chosen + max_even_rest)
        if min_even_chosen is not None and max_odd_rest is not None:
            ans = max(ans, curr_sum - min_even_chosen + max_odd_rest)

        return ans
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) sorting descending and parity adjustment
complexity.notes: Pick top k elements. If sum is odd, swap minimum odd with maximum remaining even, or vice versa.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all C(N, k) combinations takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting once allows greedy selection and constant parity adjustments.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should check the parity of top k elements and consider single swaps.
